detailed_description: The JWT Debugger is a specialized tool for decoding, validating, and analyzing JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) at a granular level. It parses tokens into their three-part structure (header, payload, signature), performs cryptographic signature verification using HMACSHA256 or RSA algorithms, and validates claims against RFC 7519 standards. Developers can inspect base64url-decoded components, check token expiration (exp), issuer (iss), and audience (aud) claims, and verify signature integrity using either a shared secret or public key. The tool’s advanced validation engine detects common security misconfigurations, such as missing signature checks or improperly formatted JWK headers. This tool addresses critical use cases: debugging authentication failures in OAuth2 flows, validating tokens generated by third-party services, auditing token security for regulatory compliance, and troubleshooting time-sensitive claims in distributed systems. Internally, it uses Node.js crypto libraries to reconstruct the signing input string, compares computed signatures against stored values, and flags discrepancies in token structure or cryptographic padding.
usage_steps: Paste a JWT string into the 'Token Input' field; the tool automatically separates header, payload, and signature segments.
Click 'Decode Components' to reveal base64url-decoded JSON objects for header and payload.
Select 'Verify Signature' and choose an algorithm (HS256, RS256, etc.) to validate the cryptographic signature.
Input a secret key or upload a PEM-encoded public key to perform signature validation against asymmetric/symmetric encryption.
Review the 'Claims Analysis' section for automated checks on expiration time (exp), not-before (nbf), and issuer (iss) claims.
Use the 'Validation Report' tab to export results or identify security risks like missing signature headers (alg: 'none').
usage_examples: A developer debugging an OAuth2 flow discovers their RS256-signed JWT fails validation due to an incorrect public key modulus length, which the tool identifies through JWK comparison.
An API maintainer confirms a third-party service's JWT contains an unexpected 'jti' (JWT ID) claim, revealing potential replay attack vulnerabilities during token validation.
A security auditor identifies a token with an extended 48-hour expiration (exp) claim exceeding organizational policies by analyzing the decoded payload timestamp.
A mobile app engineer troubleshoots session timeouts by validating the 'nbf' (not-before) claim against their system's clock drift tolerance settings.
verifyNote: Note: Signature verification is done client-side
